summary: Competitive brief synthesized from 3 research streams (frameworks /4, coding agents /5, DAG-PM /6). Verdict: product core (DAG + subagent dispatch + dashboard + exit-2 enforcement) is now largely DUPLICATED by native Claude Code (Agent Teams v2.1.32+: shared task list, auto-unblocking blocking deps, file-locked claim, TaskCreated/Completed hooks; + dynamic workflows; + commoditized 'Mission Control' dashboards in Devin/Cursor/Copilot/Factory). ~70% re-skin. Defensible moat = 3 things native lacks: (1) persistent cross-session + cross-workspace DAG with ghost edges (native teams are ephemeral, one-at-a-time, no resume), (2) typed context edges + two-tier token-economic context handoff (native = blocking only), (3) always-on graph-spanning PreToolUse gate + prompt router. Weak vs market on durable execution (Temporal/MAF/Inngest) + observability (LangSmith/Traces) + maturity. Recommendation: reposition from 'orchestrator' to 'cross-workspace context & governance layer ON TOP of Claude Code Agent Teams'; stop competing on DAG/dispatch/dashboard. Existential risk: Anthropic adding cross-session/workspace to Agent Teams. CAVEAT: verdict hinges on web-research claims about native Claude Code features — should be directly verified before acting.
